Passive Items (also referred to as Passive Weapons) are non-weapon items that give the player bonuses to their stats, similar to PowerUps. They are offered to the player alongside weapons whenever the player levels up.

The player has 6 slots for passive items, meaning that they can select up to 6 non-gift passive items from level ups. Though Mini Crewmates take up a passive item slot, they can be selected after reaching the passive limit.

The base game has 21 passive items, 17 of which are normal passive items and 4 of which are special passive items. In addition, there are 13 passive items that are only available in DLCs: 1 from the Tides of the Foscari DLC, 8 from the Emergency Meeting DLC, 1 from the Operation Guns DLC, 2 from the Ode to Castlevania DLC, and 1 from the Ante Chamber DLC, bringing the total number of passive items in the game to 34.

There are certain passive items in the game referred to as "special passive items", which cannot appear normally from the level-up choices and must be collected from a stage or by fulfilling set conditions in order to obtain them. The Emergency Meeting DLC introduces a group of new passive items known as mini crewmates. Each of them are exclusive to a certain Emergency Meeting DLC weapon, and only occur in item pool once matching weapon reaches certain level. Instead of stat bonus, they provide a hidden weapon and a pet that follows the character. All of evolutions from this DLC needs maxing out both weapon and the exclusive mini crewmate, and the mini crewmate will be consumed in evolution (the pet will be kept).

The Operation Guns DLC introduces a new passive items named Weapon Power-Up. It will only occur in item pool after taking any Operation Guns DLC weapon, and evolving each of these weapon needs to consume one Weapon Power-Up. Weapon Power-Up will occur in item pool again after previous one being consumed.

When picked, Weapon Power-Up upgrades a random weapon and gives +1 revival to the character. It won't be counted by inventory in the passive item limit and can be acquired even if the character has reached the passive item limit.
The Ode to Castlevania DLC introduces real, AI-controlled familiars (secondary characters) to the game. They can be obtained by taking a

or via certain characters' passive features. Familiars won't be counted by inventory slot in the passive item limit, and will level up along with the character. Each Familiar has its own starting weapons, its own leveling up options (which are limited and randomly picked), and won't take damage. A character can get multiple copies of the same Familiar.

The Ante Chamber DLC introduces a single passive item that is used to evolve all of the base weapons from this DLC, as long as it is at max level. It will appear in your inventory automatically once you obtain any Ante Chamber weapons, and doesn't take passive item slot.

Upon moving to an item, it can be picked up or discarded. If the player already has the item, it grants a free level if not at max level. If they already have 6 or more passive items, it becomes an additional passive item and can be thereafter upgraded from level ups. If discarded, the item disappears and can no longer be picked up. If the item was already
, either from the Collection menu or during the run, picking it up will show a third "unbanish" option. This picks up the item and allows it to be levelled again as normal.

Each hidden stage item is guarded by an Atlantean that spawns when any player gets close to the item. The player does not have to defeat the guard to pick up the item, but they will continue to follow the player until defeated. If the stage item was attracted using
, the guard will not appear until the item is interacted with.
By approaching near the item without picking it up (prior to obtaining Mad Groove (VIII)), If it is later picked up from Mad Groove, a second Atlantean can be spawned for each hidden stage item.

, and
. Save items that you only get for evolutions like
, etc. for after you already have a clear direction of your build.
If the passive item you need for your build is already a stage item, take it after you have filled your passive item slots to get the most benefit out of all of them.

However, there are situations where a stage item is too far from your initial location and selecting it early from level-up choices would be a better decision. This is the case for items where it is needed to evolve a weapon, or for items that are necessary to save your current run from an imminent game-over.
